text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI

- U.S. to give $100 million to Jordan, President Bill Clinton praises efforts of King Hussein to encourage peace. Crown Prince Hassan discusses Middle East with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and due to meet Clinton today.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali kicks off Arab tour next Saturday, including United Arab Emirates, Tunisia, Bahrain and Egypt.
- Jordan and United States to formally sign investment incentive agreement next week.
- Opposition parties call for special session of parliament to discuss U.S. congressional decision to move embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem.
AL-DUSTOUR
- Cabinet adds tourism, educational and film projects to items covered by law encouraging investment.
- Crown Prince Hassan, in news conference with Albright, calls for words to be converted into action in Middle East.
- New law allows government employees 10 years unpaid leave if they want to work in private sector or outside Jordan.
- A number of Jordanian banks expected to merge in next few months to produce bigger, stronger banks, sources say.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- Albright announces $100 million aid to Jordan.
AL-ASWAQ
- Opposition parties to name their candidates for parliamentary elections at the end of the month.
- Hong Kong and Shanghai Bank to lead manage Jordan Phosphate company's $100 million eurobond.
JORDAN TIMES
- U.S. launches long-term fund to help Jordan implement reforms.
- Princess Aysha says female military recruits in Jordan's army have higher educational background than males in same ranks.
- Jordan to hand over West Bank maps to Palestinian National Authority and train Palestinian engineers.
